messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: abnormal KV cache growth in region eu-central-1 for model-family/awq-7b-int8. kv_cache_entries up 5.8x in 10m, paging_reads/sec rising, error_rate on cont-batcher 1.1%. Auto-pager triggered to oncall.

Alice (oncall): seeing the alert in PagerDuty. Latency tail spikes ~600ms for some routes; a few customers report timeouts. Which deploys touched kernel selection recently?

Bob (eng-runtime): kernel-selector rollout 2026.3.8 touched eu-central-1 at 03:12UTC; it prefers awq-int8 kernels for lower compute. We rolled a heuristics change to prefer awq for short sequences. That could be the change.

Carla (eng-ml): note: AWQ-int8 path keeps extra per-token quant metadata in KV. Under normal batching it was okay, but if batch-merging is aggressive we can multiply KV footprint. Expected 10-30% increase, not 5-6x. Suggest looking at cont-batcher merge behavior.

Dawn (sre): node metrics show host swap IOPS up and nvme latency climbing on host-21 and host-22. Evictions hitting 90% reclaim attempts. Paging errors correlated with cont-batcher eviction loop.

Eve (support): Customer X in eu region opened a severity-2 ticket: "intermittent timeouts on inference, retries increase cost". CS escalating to enterprise ops.

Alice (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) emergency throttle on awq model routes in eu-central-1; 2) set kernel selector to prefer fp16 for awq-7b in region; 3) reduce cont-batcher merge window and max_tokens to stop super-batches. Also will notify customers. Anyone object?

Grace (oncall-backup): backing Alice. If we rollback kernel selector we should do it as a region override to avoid global churn.

Bob (eng-runtime): region override command (one-liner):

```
redctl set-config --region eu-central-1 runtime.kernel_selector.order="fp16,awq-int8" && redctl rollout service cont-batcher --region eu-central-1 --strategy rolling
```

Also a quick cont-batcher patch to reduce merge size:

```
# temporary config
continuous_batcher:
  max_merged_requests: 8   # was 32
  merge_window_ms: 6       # was 25
  max_batch_tokens: 8192   # was 32768
```

Dawn (sre): I'll cordon host-21, drain cont-batcher pods and restart after Bob's override is active. Will do one host at a time.

Carla (eng-ml): quick repro: ran synthetic workload with AWQ-int8 + large merge and saw kv_entries jump 4.7x vs fp16. The quant index buffer is duplicated per-merged-prefix; there's a leaking code path in the prefix-dedupe cache. Filing ML mitigations.

Bob (eng-runtime): override applied at 2241234720; cont-batcher rolling restart kicked off. Rolling 1 pod every 50s to reduce pressure.

incident-bot: deployment: cont-batcher rollout initiated by bob_runtime at 2241234720. 0/10 pods updated.

Dawn (sre): drain/cordon on host-21 started. Observed immediate decrease in paging latency after first pod on host-21 restarted. Monitoring stats.

Henry (cust-success): notified Customer X with templated update: "We're investigating higher latency in eu-central-1 affecting a subset of requests; engineering is applying mitigations now." Customer asked for ETA; provided 2h provisional window.

Alice (oncall): also enabling temporary per-tenant rate caps for enterprise tenants in region to protect Dedicated pools. Applying conservative caps.

Bob (eng-runtime): per-tenant caps applied. Also logging shows cont-batcher had a bug where merged-prefix dedupe cache kept stale quant-index references after eviction. That would amplify memory usage beyond per-request expectation.

Carla (eng-ml): adding detail: AWQ stores per-layer quant index arrays; the dedupe cache previously held strong refs to these arrays when merging prefixes; when eviction attempted the refs prevented reclaim. Patch idea: use weakrefs + reference counting or prune cache entries for quant arrays when merge_count > threshold.

Dawn (sre): after second pod restart, paging_reads/sec down 70%, kv_cache_entries trending to baseline. Error rate dropped to 0.15%.

incident-bot: update at 2241234900: mitigations reduced pressure. Monitoring window started.

Alice (oncall): good. Owners and next steps: Bob - keep the selector override for region and prepare runtime hotfix to change cache lifecycle (48h). Carla - prototype quant-index pruning and add regression tests (72h). Dawn - finish rolling restarts and validate nodes stable (2h). Eve/Henry - track customer comms and SLA exposure. I'll collect timeline for postmortem.

Bob (eng-runtime): creating ticket INT-2026-221: runtime selector rollback + cache lifecycle change. Will include unit tests to simulate merge patterns. Target patch in 36-48h if no regressions.

Carla (eng-ml): creating ticket ML-2026-142: AWQ quant-index weakref/prune. ETA 72h with benchmarks. Also will add a feature flag to disable heavy-index caching per-model.

Eve (support): Customer X acknowledged workaround and asked to be notified when fix scheduled. We provided link to status page and ETA.

Alice (oncall): moving incident to monitoring. Keep channel open for any relapses. If something flares, escalate to oncall lead and execs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring at 2241234975. Monitoring window 2h. Tags: awq-int8, kv-cache, cont-batch, kernel-selector, paging.

Dawn (sre): adding follow-up dashboards for postmortem: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv/kv-overview?var-region=eu-central-1 and https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/infra/paging?var-host=host-21

Bob (eng-runtime): log excerpt after override (sanitized):

```
[INFO] kernel_selector override active: fp16 first
[INFO] cont-batcher config: max_merged_requests=8, merge_window_ms=6
[WARN] kv_cache_eviction: reclaimed 640MB on host-21
```

Alice (oncall): thanks all. I'll write a short incident summary and link tickets. Grace, please take lead if this reappears.

Grace (oncall-backup): will monitor. :ok_hand:

incident-bot: thread pinned for postmortem ingestion."
